text.p: Dhaka stocks ended sharply down amid mounting selling pressure by investors fearing further falls on the news of poor company performances, brokers said.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange all-share price index dropped 37.93 points or 4.21 percent to 862.05 on turnover of 50 million taka. Losers led gainers by 117 to 15.
"We are receiving only sell orders from investors. The investors are wary about the future of the market as there is no sign of any recovery," said broker Moshtaque Ahmed.
Brokers said many companies including Apex Footware, Dynamic Textiles and Kashem Drycell Ltd either reported poor results or refused to offer dividend for the year 1996.

The downward readjustment of Bangladesh taka against the dollar on Monday, the second time since July, by more than one percent to 44.45/65 also had a negative impact on trading in the market, brokers said.

"There is virtually panic selling by retailers. Investors' sentiment has hit a new low amid companies showing bad fianancial results and frequent devaluation of the local currency," said another broker.
Olympic Industries lost 43 taka to 408, Beximco Pharma fell 6.25 to 116.08 and Bata Shoe declined 5.38 to 104.81.
